checkOutcomes.method: compare heap snapshots for retained growth - a baseline, then one taken after repeating the interaction with `--interact` about 10x (the memory-tracer methodology: baseline -> repeat -> post -> compare). Performance.getMetrics (JSHeapUsedSize, Nodes) across the same before/after window is corroboration. If Chrome DevTools MCP is available, follow its memory-leak-debugging skill: capture baseline, target, and final snapshots, then use memlab or the provided comparison workflow rather than reading raw .heapsnapshot files directly. The package-native `heap` primitive remains the default path. This check is only meaningful where the page has a real interaction to repeat; for a static page with none, mark it not-applicable with a rationale rather than fabricating one. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Evidence linked to F20: Heap summary rises from 681,854 nodes/36.57 MB to 748,416 nodes/39.91 MB after ten top-to-bottom scroll cycles. Lazy content may explain part of the 9% growth, so confidence is low.

checkOutcomes.method: a single `heap` summary's totals (nodeCount, totalSelfSizeBytes, constructor population) plus Performance.getMetrics (Nodes, JSHeapUsedSize) give the current footprint to judge against the page's purpose. Chrome DevTools MCP heap snapshots and memlab snapshot analysis can provide the same memory distribution when available. Read summaries or derived analysis, never raw snapshots unless a dedicated heap-analysis tool is doing the analysis. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Baseline heap is 36.57 MB for a media-rich listing; post-scroll is 39.91 MB, still bounded within the observed session.

checkOutcomes.method: the `heap` summary by constructor (Detached* nodes) compared across a before/after pair shows a growing detached-DOM population; an `evaluate` probe can sample listener/timer counts (e.g. getEventListeners-style counting, or instrumenting addEventListener/setInterval) before and after the repeated interaction to spot growth. Chrome DevTools MCP heap snapshots plus the memory-leak-debugging skill's common-leak guidance can corroborate detached DOM, listeners, closures, globals, and unbounded caches. Caveat from the memory-tracer and Chrome DevTools MCP guidance: detached nodes can be intentional caches, so judge confidence rather than asserting a bug. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Neither heap summary surfaced Detached* constructors among its top retained constructors; no runaway task activity was observed.

paths.description: Homepage and media listing, the primary discovery surface; tested at desktop, 360x800, dark/reduced-motion, no-JS, and after consent rejection.
Category/listing archetype, representing taxonomy and repeated media cards.
Video detail/player archetype, representing the core watch journey without starting playback.
Account-entry flow, inspected through the first sign-up choice and disclosures without submitting personal data.
Representative HTTP failure and recovery surface.

findings.summary: Site theme does not declare or adapt the browser color scheme
findings.evidence: Under emulated dark preference the page stays on its fixed dark theme, while computed `color-scheme` is `normal`; the dark and default screenshots are effectively identical.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare `color-scheme` and bind surface/text tokens to `prefers-color-scheme` or `light-dark()` so browser UI and both preferences are handled.

findings.summary: Loading shimmer continues under reduced-motion
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe reports eight running `shimmer-56cf2` animations at 2,000 ms while `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is active.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable nonessential shimmer/transition animation in a reduced-motion media query, retaining only necessary state feedback.

findings.summary: Route changes have no view-transition treatment
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM/CSS contains no view-transition usage although the site has many cross-document navigation paths; detail/category changes are abrupt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document view transitions for stable shared chrome and preserve an immediate fallback.

findings.summary: Consent interstitial obscures the primary content on arrival
findings.evidence: Desktop capture shows a large consent surface covering the content and controls before interaction; it is also present in the crawler/no-JS view.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep legally required consent concise, accessible, and non-obscuring where possible; expose equivalent accept/reject controls and preserve access to essential content.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is not exposed as a semantic dialog
findings.evidence: A visible modal dominates the initial screenshot, but the DOM probe finds no `<dialog>`, `[role=dialog]`, or `[aria-modal=true]` on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use `<dialog>` (or a correctly labelled modal dialog) with focus containment, Escape/platform dismissal where permitted, and focus restoration.

findings.summary: Primary templates are fixed-width and unusable at 360 px
findings.evidence: Mobile layout reports 1,030 px content width against a 360 px visual viewport, 670 px horizontal overflow. Homepage, category, detail, and signup captures all clip primary content offscreen.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the fixed desktop canvas with fluid layout constraints, wrapping navigation, responsive grids/player sizing, and test every primary template at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Loading performance misses the LCP target and ships a large script chain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 4.5 s LCP. HAR records 140 requests and 1.80 MB transferred, including 62 scripts/1.06 MB; Lighthouse estimates 1,130 ms render-blocking savings and trace records 145 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, inline/split critical CSS, defer nonessential code and third parties, and remove unused CSS/JS identified by coverage.

findings.summary: Media cards waste bytes and omit intrinsic dimensions
findings.evidence: Image audit finds 29/36 images without width/height, 14 oversized, 14 legacy-format results, and eight below-fold images not lazy loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions/aspect-ratio, correctly sized `srcset` candidates, modern formats, and lazy-load below-fold media while prioritising only the LCP image.

findings.summary: Interactive controls have weak keyboard focus and undersized targets
findings.evidence: Computed focus styles for search/login buttons report no outline, 53 visible controls are under 24 px in one dimension, and Lighthouse fails target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast `:focus-visible` indicator and enlarge/space pointer targets to at least the applicable accessibility target guidance.

findings.summary: Accessible names and semantic structure contain failures
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails button-name, label/content-name mismatch, list structure, and accessibility-tree audits; the probe also finds an unlabeled category filter input.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a programmatic name matching visible text, use valid list children and landmarks, and verify the resulting accessibility tree.

findings.summary: Text and links fail contrast requirements
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 13 color-contrast failures and one link-in-text-block failure; no prefers-contrast handling was found in the captured CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise foreground/background contrast, add a non-color link affordance, and preserve control/text distinction under increased/forced contrast.

findings.summary: Zoom/reflow and touch accessibility fail together
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails the meta-viewport zoom audit and target-size; independent 360 px captures show severe clipping instead of reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not cap page zoom, make layouts reflow at 320 CSS px/400% zoom, and enlarge crowded controls.

findings.summary: Indexing metadata is incomplete for a large catalogue
findings.evidence: robots.txt is available, but `/sitemap.xml` returns 404; the canonical points to a different hostname (`hi.xhamster.desi`) than the audited host.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish sitemap index files for public catalogue URLs and ensure each host variant intentionally canonicalises to a reachable preferred URL.

findings.summary: Shareable and structured metadata is absent on the entry page
findings.evidence: The rendered probe finds zero JSON-LD blocks and zero Open Graph tags despite a content-heavy media catalogue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add content-accurate schema.org JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata to homepage, category, and detail templates.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookies leave avoidable gaps
findings.evidence: Headers lack `X-Content-Type-Options` and `Referrer-Policy`; CSP is only `frame-ancestors`; two first-party cookies are not Secure and `settings` uses SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Send nosniff and a strict referrer policy, expand CSP beyond frame control, and mark HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest suitable SameSite/HttpOnly settings.

findings.summary: Third-party activity occurs before a consent decision
findings.evidence: Tracker/network captures observe 14 third-party origins and 117 third-party requests transferring 1.69 MB on initial load, while the consent interstitial is still awaiting a choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate nonessential third-party requests on an explicit consent state, minimise vendors/data, and self-host or defer assets where practical.

findings.summary: Account entry offers federated sign-in but no modern phishing-resistant option
findings.evidence: The signup surface exposes Google, X, and email choices, while the inspected DOM has no WebAuthn/passkey affordance. No permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration/authentication alongside existing options and request permissions only from an explanatory user action.

findings.summary: Core content degrades noticeably without JavaScript
findings.evidence: Discoverability finds 63% rendered-word coverage without JavaScript; the crawler capture adds a prominent JavaScript-required warning and still shows the consent surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render essential listings/navigation and make consent/basic browsing progressively enhanced so non-JS and failing-script states retain the core task.

findings.summary: Consent choice and pre-consent loading undermine trustworthy defaults
findings.evidence: The page asks users to accept/reject cookies, yet HAR/trackers record substantial third-party traffic before either choice; this makes the stated control less effective.
findings.suggestedFix: Default nonessential processing off, keep choices equally legible, and make the observed network state match the user’s consent decision.

findings.summary: Retained heap grows after repeated feed traversal
findings.evidence: Heap summary rises from 681,854 nodes/36.57 MB to 748,416 nodes/39.91 MB after ten top-to-bottom scroll cycles. Lazy content may explain part of the 9% growth, so confidence is low.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat baseline/target/final snapshots in one session, force GC between snapshots, and investigate retained feed cards, observers, listeners, and caches if growth continues.
